A slower rhythm, under an island sky.
The idea

Meet one another. Try something unfamiliar. See what you might discover.

The Farmhouse is shaped around shared experience. Share stories, encounter local culture, learn side by side, and give each other room to grow. There is no single right way to take part—just an invitation to be curious, live independently and together, and discover what a little openness can bring.

The place, honestly

Nature has the run of it.

Six simple units, a stream nearby, chickens underfoot, and trees doing what trees do. This is a living farmhouse, not a resort pretending to be somewhere else.

Open to the island air

Thatched roofs, wood floors, and natural ventilation through open spaces below the roof—including in the bathrooms.

Small comforts, shared life

Gather when you like.
Find quiet when you need.

An open common kitchen, hammocks, green corners to sit in, and a place for a fire or barbecue. Premium units have an attached kitchen. Fast internet keeps you connected when you need it.

A nature-oriented stay

Open to island air.

Thatched roofs, timber floors and natural ventilation keep the rooms connected to their tropical setting, including the bathrooms. There is a stream nearby, and chickens, geckos, frogs and insects are part of life here. There is no air conditioning. The Farmhouse suits people who enjoy an open-air stay and feel comfortable sharing space with nature.

A life painted in many places.
A little about Peter

He left. He lived.
He came home.

Peter was 18 when he left Vietnam. Canada and Europe became part of his life; so did years of seeing the world from somewhere else. Eventually he returned to Vietnam and made room for the thing that has always called him: painting.

The Farmhouse began as Peter’s dream of creating a place he could share. It was never only a commercial idea. He wanted people to step away from familiar routines, spend time close to nature, and try something new—whether that means painting, taking photographs, learning, moving gently, or simply being together.

He hopes the Farmhouse can welcome Vietnamese locals, travelers and expats, along with artists, photographers, writers and people bringing a workshop or gathering idea. Beneath all of it is a simple hope: that people leave with more room for self-understanding, generosity and connection with one another.

Peter still paints here among the trees, making contemporary abstract art. His own creative life remains part of the Farmhouse, alongside the many different ways people may choose to use the place.

A dream made into a place to share.

No surprises, please

What this place is—and isn’t.

You might love it here if…

  • You like being close to nature and don't mind its sounds and small surprises.
  • You enjoy simple spaces, fresh air, and a little time away from routine.
  • You are open to shared places and the company of other curious people.
  • You want to make, learn, explore—or simply slow down.

You may prefer somewhere else if…

  • You need air conditioning or fully enclosed, climate-controlled rooms.
  • You want a polished resort service and a tightly planned programme.
  • Geckos, frogs, chickens, insects, or the possibility of other crawling visitors would make you uneasy.
  • You need to reach town on foot; the farmhouse is a little inland, so plan your own transport.
A small map in words

Five kilometres
from Cua Can.

The Farmhouse sits in the green, a little off the main road and about 5 km from Cua Can town. Close enough to head out and explore; tucked far enough in to feel a little removed from the everyday.

Because it is interior, guests need a bike, motorbike, or car to get around comfortably. Exact directions can be shared when your visit is arranged.

For artists · hosts · curious people

Bring people together around something you care about.

The Farmhouse welcomes small gatherings for artists, photographers, writers, facilitators and people with a skill or story to share. Propose a workshop, a shared meal, a photo walk or another thoughtful way to bring people together.

With six stays, an open common kitchen, green gathering spaces and fast internet, the Farmhouse can support intimate, hands-on experiences. Tell Peter your idea, who it is for and what you need; the details are arranged together before anything is confirmed.
